releases.title: Silent Antigravity updater, real Mermaid diagrams & smarter schedules
releases.summary: A fix release for the papercuts you actually saw: Antigravity no longer flashes a console window in the background, code blocks and Mermaid diagrams render with a proper header row, a pinned thread shows exactly one pin, and thread-bound schedules follow the thread's current agent.

changes.label: Antigravity
changes.text: Background terminal windows no longer flash open when Antigravity runs — the CLI's update check is kept fresh so its background updater never spawns a console.

changes.label: Chat
changes.text: Code blocks now have a header row — language label on the left, copy button on the right — instead of a floating button covering the first line.

changes.label: Chat
changes.text:
Mermaid diagrams render as real flowcharts again, including multi-line node labels that use
, instead of showing raw source text.

changes.label: Chat
changes.text: The token speed readout now appears for every agent — providers that stream in big chunks or reopen from history fall back to a whole-turn estimate.

changes.label: Sidebar
changes.text: A pinned thread shows a single pin affordance — the trailing pin button doubles as the indicator and the unpin control.

changes.label: Schedules
changes.text: A schedule bound to a thread follows that thread's current agent and model — switching the thread no longer sends the old model to the new harness.

changes.label: Usage
changes.text: Codex cards put the 5-hour session bar first, and the backup gpt-reserve pool is labeled GPT Reserve instead of a raw slug.

changes.label: Grok
changes.text: Grok builds that don't report MCP capability still get CraftStation's built-in MCP servers, so scheduled runs can actually use the Schedule tools.

releases.title: Antigravity answers settle on the authoritative response; cleaner markdown tables and math
releases.summary:
Antigravity turns no longer show a duplicated regenerated reply — the terminal result frame now replaces the stream with the provider's authoritative response instead of appending to it. Table cells render
as a real line break, and display-math blocks whose closing $$ shares the last content line render through KaTeX instead of leaking raw source.

changes.label: Antigravity
changes.text: A regenerated second answer no longer gets appended after the real reply — the terminal result response replaces the assistant stream, dropping retracted text.

changes.label: Chat
changes.text: tags inside markdown table cells render as line breaks instead of literal text.

changes.label: Chat
changes.text: Display-math blocks whose closing $$ is glued to the last content line (…\end{bmatrix}$$) render as formulas instead of raw source.

releases.title: Skill names accept underscores; quieter thread rows
releases.summary: Skills named with underscores (my_interview, _private_skill) now import, validate, and invoke through the composer, and sidebar thread rows show their full title by default with pin/more/archive actions revealed only on hover.

changes.label: Skills
changes.text: Skill names with underscores are no longer filtered out — they import cleanly, pass validation, and bind through / or $ invocation in the composer.

changes.label: Sidebar
changes.text: Thread rows show their full title by default; the pin, more, and archive actions stay hidden until the row is hovered or focused, matching project rows.

releases.title: Locked-CLI updates land; cleaner update feedback
releases.summary: Updates that download large bundles or replace a running binary now complete: downloads get a 30-minute window, staged builds swap in via rename while the process runs, and update output no longer shows raw terminal escapes.

changes.label: Updates
changes.text: Devin can finally update — its installer downloads ~180MB and ends by overwriting a running exe, so the 5-minute timeout killed the download and the copy failed on the file lock. Downloads get 30 minutes, and the staged build is swapped in via rename instead.

changes.label: Updates
changes.text: Update failure messages no longer show raw terminal escape sequences as garbage characters.

changes.label: Updates
changes.text: Running an update against a CLI that is already at the latest version no longer reports a failure — the no-op is recognized as success.

releases.title: Update success is verified, shadowed CLIs heal
releases.summary: CLI updates now prove the resolved binary actually changed before reporting success, and stale foreign executables that shadow a package-managed install are removed so the real update takes effect.

changes.label: Updates
changes.text: An update that exits successfully without changing the resolved binary no longer reports success — the post-update version probe reports an honest failure instead, so the entry stays listed instead of pretending it landed.

changes.label: Updates
changes.text: CLIs shadowed by a stale executable in the npm global folder now self-heal: Windows resolves the orphan .exe ahead of the managed .cmd shim, so package updates never took effect — the orphan is removed so the managed binary answers.

releases.title: CLI updates actually land, stale entries clear
releases.summary: Two fixes for the update menu: Devin's update now runs the real installer instead of an advisory command that only printed instructions, and CLIs whose version moved outside the menu's own flow stop listing as outdated.

changes.label: Updates
changes.text: Devin updates no longer report success without changing anything — its built-in update command is advisory-only, so CraftStation now verifies the version actually changed and falls through to the official installer when it didn't.

changes.label: Updates
changes.text: A CLI that updated outside the menu's own flow (background detection or an external install) no longer keeps listing as outdated — the update check now re-runs whenever a detected installed version changes.

releases.title: Update badge clears after a landed update
releases.summary: A small fix for the update indicator that kept showing a pending update after the CLI had already been updated.

changes.label: Updates
changes.text: The titlebar update badge no longer stays lit after a CLI update lands — the post-update re-check now compares against the freshly detected version instead of a stale snapshot.

releases.title: A real follow-up queue & tidier thread header
releases.summary: Queueing a message while a thread is working now stacks every message instead of silently replacing the previous one, and the pane close button sits where window controls belong.

changes.label: Threads
changes.text: You can queue as many follow-up messages as you like — each gets its own row above the composer and sends in order when the turn settles, with Send now, Edit and Delete per message.

changes.label: Threads
changes.text: Queueing a second message no longer overwrites the first — older messages stay queued and send before newer ones, and a failed send restores the message at the front instead of dropping it.

changes.label: Threads
changes.text: The pane close button moved to the far right of the thread header, after the pop-out control, so it no longer sits on the status capsule.

releases.title: Real output tokens from every harness
releases.summary: The tok/s reading now prefers each harness's own token counters — Codex, Claude, OpenCode, Kimi, Grok, Cursor, Pi, Command Code, Muse and DeepSeek all report their real output where the CLI exposes it — and generation time is stamped where the provider emits it, so batching delays can't inflate the rate.

changes.label: Threads
changes.text: The output-speed reading no longer explodes into the thousands: provider usage samples are attributed per message segment and evolving snapshots replace instead of accumulate, so a Codex or OpenCode usage push is never double-counted.

changes.label: Threads
changes.text: Decode time is now measured from when the provider emitted each delta, not when the UI got around to processing it — IPC and background batching can no longer compress the window and fake a faster rate.

changes.label: Threads
changes.text: Every harness that reports real output tokens now feeds the figure directly — Codex (both lanes), Claude, OpenCode (both paths), Cursor, Pi, Command Code, Muse, and DeepSeek included; providers with no per-call counter keep the clearly-marked character estimate.

releases.title: Output speed reading now uses provider-reported tokens
releases.summary: The tok/s figure on a thread's status indicator is now measured the way DeepSeek Harness measures it: real per-model-call output tokens over per-segment decode windows, instead of a character estimate spread across the whole turn.

changes.label: Threads
changes.text: The output-speed reading no longer collapses on tool-heavy turns. Decode time is now summed per streaming segment (first delta to last delta of each message), so tool execution and waiting never count as generation time — a 52-second turn with tool calls used to show ~2 tok/s because the whole turn wall-clock was the denominator.

changes.label: Threads
changes.text: The numerator is now real: provider-reported output + reasoning tokens from each model call's usage sample replace the character estimate, with the estimate covering only text streamed since the last sample. The rate moved off the status pill into the hover details panel, and the estimate marker only shows when no provider numbers have arrived.

releases.title: Account pools rotate on 5-hour and weekly quota axes
releases.summary: Codex and Kimi pool accounts now track the rolling 5-hour window and the weekly budget independently: a Plus account that hits its 5-hour limit steps aside for the next account and rejoins the pool automatically when the window resets.

changes.label: Account Pools
changes.text: Codex Plus accounts that hit the 5-hour usage limit are now actually rotated out: the turn-level quota error is recorded as a per-axis block with its own reset time, so the pool skips that account until the window rolls over — previously Plus never reported the 5h window to the usage poller, so the account looked healthy and kept burning failed turns. Live rate-limit pushes from the app-server land on the bound account in both chat and crafted lanes.

changes.label: Account Pools
changes.text: Quota recovery is now evidence-driven: a healthy usage poll can no longer erase a still-live 5h block, a lagged percentage can't un-mark an axis a failed turn just exhausted, and expired windows heal the account on their own. Disabled and auth-expired rows are never silently revived. Kimi gets the same 5h/weekly treatment through its 402/403 quota classifier.

changes.label: Threads
changes.text: The working indicator now shows a live output speed estimate (≈ 42 tok/s) — the average decode rate across the turn, ignoring tool-call gaps. It's computed from streamed text and marked as an estimate; billing numbers still come only from provider-reported counters.

releases.title: Gemini answers no longer end mid-sentence
releases.summary: A one-fix patch: Gemini/Antigravity replies could visually stop mid-list-item (e.g. at "1. *") because a mid-turn rewritten snapshot of the same answer was appended after the already-complete text.

changes.label: Antigravity
changes.text: Gemini/Antigravity replies no longer look cut off mid-sentence: when the CLI rewrites the answer mid-turn and sends a snapshot of the revised variant, the dedup now detects that the candidate slice replays text the stream already showed and appends nothing — the complete answer you saw streaming is what stays. Short coincidental head/tail matches (a shared "*" or digit) also no longer truncate deltas.

releases.title: Thread rename actually opens
releases.summary: A patch release: renaming a thread in the sidebar finally works for threads shown in more than one section, Antigravity/Gemini answers no longer repeat when status lines get folded into the final snapshot, and managed Grok binaries stop doubling their disk footprint.

changes.label: Threads
changes.text: Rename now opens and commits reliably: when a thread appears in several sidebar sections (project list, Workspace inbox, Pinned), only the row you clicked enters edit mode — previously every duplicate row mounted an input at once and the focus race cancelled the rename within a frame.

changes.label: Antigravity
changes.text: Gemini/Antigravity replies no longer render twice: the CLI's closing snapshot can embed already-streamed status lines in the middle of the response (a superseded draft, queued notices, then the regenerated answer), and the dedup now cuts the response at the last replayed stretch — not only at prefix or suffix boundaries — so just the final answer is appended.

changes.label: Grok
changes.text: Managed account-pool binaries now hardlink the versioned copy instead of duplicating it (~150 MB saved per profile), and each update cleans up superseded versions and parked swap files.

releases.title: Automatic CLI updates & a real Grok fix
releases.summary: A patch release: agent CLIs can now keep themselves up to date, Grok updates finally reach the binaries your account-pool sessions actually run, and manual thread renames stick.

changes.label: Updates
changes.text: Settings → Agents → General gains Auto-update CLIs, on by default — when a version check finds a newer release, each agent CLI updates through the same pipeline as the titlebar menu; turning it off keeps checks read-only.

changes.label: Grok
changes.text: Updating Grok now refreshes the per-account managed binaries your sessions actually launch — previously pool profiles stayed pinned to their first-installed build and kept reporting the CLI as outdated after a successful update.

changes.label: Threads
changes.text: Renaming a thread actually sticks: titles now track who named them, so an auto-generated title arriving late can no longer overwrite your rename.

releases.title: Third-party models on DeepSeek Harness, math & crash fixes
releases.summary: A patch release: third-party and OpenCode Go models now run correctly on DeepSeek Harness, malformed LaTeX formulas in chat render instead of leaking raw source, and maximizing the side panel no longer crashes the conversation view.

changes.label: DeepSeek Harness
changes.text: Third-party models now launch on DeepSeek Harness instead of failing with a model binding error — OpenCode Go catalog picks, Command Code rows, and any bound OpenAI-compatible account all get a correctly projected provider.

changes.label: Chat
changes.text: LaTeX formulas and Markdown structure in assistant messages render again, even when the model emits malformed ..$ delimiters or unbalanced braces inside a formula.

changes.label: Chat
changes.text: Maximizing the side panel no longer crashes the conversation view, and crash details are now recorded for faster diagnosis.

changes.label: Antigravity
changes.text: Gemini narration now interleaves with tool calls in true timeline order instead of collapsing into one block above all tools, and the closing response snapshot no longer duplicates the streamed answer.

releases.title: Unified capability management, OpenCode quotas & a calmer sidebar
releases.summary: CraftStation manages MCP servers and Skills as one capability layer across all supported harnesses. OpenCode Go subscription meters and balance finally load on the newer console, and the sidebar no longer shows a git badge on every project and worktree row.

changes.label: Capabilities
changes.text: Unified MCP and Skills capability foundation with Auto (enabled + compatible + available) and Efficient (Harness Profile recommended) resolution modes.

changes.label: MCP & Skills
changes.text: Imported external MCP servers and Skills are now tracked with provenance metadata, ensuring CraftStation remains the single source of truth for managed capabilities.

changes.label: Harness Injection
changes.text: Launch-time capability injection automatically filters MCP transports and skills based on harness runtime compatibility and environment support.

changes.label: Sidebar
changes.text: Project and worktree rows no longer carry a git status badge — branch and PR details stay in the Git panel, reachable from the row's context menu.

changes.label: OpenCode
changes.text: Quota windows now load for accounts on the newer console — Go subscription meters (5-hour, weekly, monthly) and your prepaid balance show correctly instead of an empty quota card.

releases.title: A tidier workbench & lighter terminals
releases.summary: The crafting workbench now uses matching square slots and a wider ingredients panel. Busy terminals use less CPU, startup cleanup runs after launch, Windows console hosts are reclaimed when their sessions end, and exhausted pool accounts hand off to the next one automatically.

changes.label: Crafting
changes.text: Model, harness, MCP and skill slots now match the crafting grid, with clearer selection highlights, enabled-state dots and a wider Ingredients panel beside more compact result and recipe cards.

changes.label: Terminals
changes.text: Large bursts of terminal output are delivered in batches, reducing CPU use while preserving the complete output and scrollback.

changes.label: Startup
changes.text: Historical output compaction and usage cleanup now run after launch, with an index that speeds up removal of expired usage records.

changes.label: Windows
changes.text: Console hosts left behind after terminal sessions close or exit naturally are now reclaimed when they can be uniquely matched to the finished session.
Production builds now monitor the main process so the supervisor also shuts down after a crash or force-close, reducing lingering background processes.

changes.label: Permissions
changes.text: Switching a thread between agents keeps your full-access choice — it no longer silently drops to Ask for approval when the two agents name the permission differently.

changes.label: Account pool
changes.text: When a ChatGPT account hits its usage limit mid-task, the thread now rotates to the next pool account and replays the prompt instead of stopping on the error.

releases.title: Windows shell preferences, sturdier ACP agents & smarter PR targets
releases.summary: You can now choose which Windows shell runs your terminals and which one CraftStation uses behind the scenes. Removing an ACP agent, opening a pull request from a worktree, and closing the app all behave the way you expect.

changes.label: Windows
changes.text: You can now choose which shell the Terminal panel opens — PowerShell 7, Windows PowerShell 5.1, or Command Prompt — pick a separate PowerShell host for agents, logins, installs, and CraftStation's internal commands, and pass extra arguments such as -NoProfile to every new terminal session.

changes.label: ACP agents
changes.text: Session modes reported by ACP agents now read as prose in the approval picker, so goose shows Smart approve instead of smart_approve.

changes.label: Codex
changes.text: New chats now start with the context window you saved for the provider, and changing a thread's context window reuses the running app server instead of spawning a second one.

An agent that reports a successful sign-in CraftStation cannot confirm now explains how to finish setup instead of showing a raw error, and an environment with a working session no longer asks you to log in again.

changes.label: ACP agents
changes.text: Removing an installed agent now stops its running threads first and clears the install folder even while Windows still holds the binary, so a stale copy no longer blocks the next install.

changes.label: Pull requests
changes.text: Creating a pull request from a worktree now resolves the base branch against your local branches, so the target branch is prefilled correctly, keeps its exact name when it collides with a remote ref, and stays selectable in the target list.

changes.label: Windows
changes.text: Closing the main window now quits CraftStation when close-to-tray is off, instead of leaving the app running with nothing on screen.

changes.label: Codex
changes.text: Closing a Codex thread while a turn is still running now interrupts that turn instead of leaving it working against the shared app server.

changes.label: Antigravity
changes.text: Antigravity sessions started from a project now bind to that project so its file tools stay scoped to the folder you opened, while Home sessions stay projectless.

releases.title: Codex context windows, Home permissions & project terminals
releases.summary: CraftStation adds configurable context windows and compaction thresholds for Codex, enables unrestricted agent sessions in your Home directory, and adds direct terminal access to project menus. Branch tracking in worktrees and ACP skill badges in the composer also get useful fixes.

changes.label: Codex
changes.text: You can now customize the context window sizes available in the Codex composer under Settings, defaulting new chats to 400k with automatic compaction starting at 95% of your chosen window.

changes.label: Projects
changes.text: You can now open a project's terminal directly from the project menu in both the grouped sidebar and flat project filter.

changes.label: Home
changes.text: Agent sessions started in the projectless Home folder now run with unrestricted permissions across all providers, allowing full read and write access across your home directory.

changes.label: Composer
changes.text: Skills invoked with slash commands in the composer and chat messages now display with a dedicated sparkles icon and accessible badge instead of generic slash-command text.

changes.label: Worktrees
changes.text: Creating a new worktree branch no longer accidentally inherits origin/main as its remote tracking upstream, preventing new worktrees from falsely reporting behind commits.

releases.title: Muse Code, Claude skills & sturdier sessions
releases.summary: CraftStation adds Muse Code as a first-class terminal agent, surfaces Claude's own skills in the composer, and keeps launches and follow-ups alive when you switch panes or a session disappears.

changes.label: Muse Code
changes.text: You can now run Meta's Muse Code CLI as a terminal session in CraftStation — pick Muse Spark models and reasoning effort, sign in from Settings, and resume where you left off. On Windows, install it through WSL.

changes.label: Claude
changes.text: Claude's own skills — the ones the CLI ships, not just files on disk — now appear in the composer slash menu and run as streaming skills instead of silent local commands.

changes.label: Threads
changes.text: Threads show a Connecting… state in the header and chat while the session is starting, so a launch no longer looks idle.
Starting a thread and switching or closing the pane no longer leaves the agent silently never started; launch failures now show as an error on the thread.

If a session is gone when you send a message — after a restart or unload — CraftStation relaunches it and delivers the prompt instead of dropping it, including from the send_to_thread MCP tool. Interrupting a thread whose session already died now settles it to Inactive instead of leaving it stuck Working.

changes.label: Codex
changes.text: Steering a running Codex turn now lands on the in-flight work instead of starting a conflicting turn, answers no longer vanish while Codex is compacting or running concurrent turns, and app-server sessions no longer stall when acquiring a server fails or two launches race.

releases.title: Agent Plugins, merged PR sync & stoppable actions
releases.summary: A big feature release: CraftStation adds a standards-based Agent Plugins marketplace, syncs merged pull request branches automatically, and lets you stop running project actions from context menus. Worktree launches, pane placement, subagent status, usage reporting, and provider reliability all get substantial polish.

changes.label: Agent Plugins
changes.text: Browse, install, and manage Agent Plugins in Settings, with bundled Browser Tools, Chrome Tools, Computer Use, GitHub, Outlook, and Subagent Delegation packages.

changes.label: Agent Plugins
changes.text: Plugin skills and MCP servers work across supported agents, can be enabled individually or invoked from composer mentions, and carry through restarts, recovery, WSL, and remote sessions.

changes.label: Worktrees
changes.text: Worktree threads launch more responsively: your message appears instantly with a live "Creating worktree…" indicator while CraftStation sets everything up.

changes.label: Pull requests
changes.text: After you merge a pull request, CraftStation pulls the merged base branch into your checkout once per project, and sync badges now appear on experiment groups, thread groups, and thread rows until the pull completes.
Stop any running project action straight from the thread, worktree, or project context menu, and running actions are tracked even after their terminal tab closes.

changes.label: MCP
changes.text: The CraftStation MCP server can identify the current thread and list or read live terminal panes with worktree-scoped scrollback, and you can @-mention Terminal in the composer when app controls are enabled.

changes.label: Subagents
changes.text: Resumed Claude subagents get their own labeled Agent Resume row, and cancelled Crossagents runs show a clear cancelled state instead of looking stuck.

changes.label: Command Code
changes.text: Usage now shows Command Code's rolling 5-hour and weekly dollar limits alongside monthly credits, with reset countdowns, matching Studio and the CLI.

changes.label: Panes
changes.text: The New thread menu lists your projects, and you can drag any of them straight onto a pane or the gap between two panes to start that project's draft exactly where you want it.

changes.label: Crossagents
changes.text: Subagent runs are named with the model's sub-provider so similar selections are easy to tell apart, the learned selections list scrolls when it grows long, and the provider filter explains that unchecked providers only opt out of automatic routing.

changes.label: Usage
changes.text: Dollar-denominated usage windows lead with the percent on the bar, and spend amounts sit next to the reset countdown as smaller muted text.

changes.label: Projects
changes.text: Project pickers now mark local and remote projects with distinct icons, and you can open GitHub Actions from a worktree group's context menu.

changes.label: Sidebar
changes.text: Collapsed worktree groups tint their icon when a thread inside is working or has finished, so you can read a group's state without expanding it.

changes.label: Composer
changes.text: The add menu is tidier: Computer Use and Experiment keep single-line rows with their descriptions moved into info tooltips.

changes.label: Panes
changes.text: Opening a pane now splits the space evenly instead of squeezing the newest one, existing panes keep their relative widths, and the insert line lights up as soon as you drag near the edge between two panes.
Renaming a thread no longer bumps it to the top of the list, completed turns stay closed when trailing plan or goal updates arrive, and the turn timer stops ticking as soon as the turn ends.

changes.label: Sidebar
changes.text: Disabled, hidden, and offline-server projects reappear in a dedicated section of the project filter so you can re-enable them, and Remove Project is disabled for servers you can't reach.
Cancelling agent detection now stops probes and cleanup promptly across every provider, and hung WSL processes are killed on timeout instead of lingering.

Kimi subscription tiers show the correct credit multipliers, an explicit Fast mode off now carries over to your next draft, and one-shot responses that leak raw tool-call markers are rejected instead of shown as text.

changes.label: Antigravity
changes.text: Every reasoning level reported by agy now appears in the model picker, including High for Gemini 3.6 Flash.

changes.label: Antigravity
changes.text: Threads created in linked Git worktrees now keep agy's file tools bound to that exact worktree instead of falling back to the main checkout.

changes.label: OpenCode
changes.text: Go plan usage now comes from your live opencode.ai subscription instead of local CLI spend, and sign-in remains available when CLI authentication has no meters, so empty local snapshots no longer strand you.

changes.label: Grok
changes.text: An explicit request to push now runs without a redundant confirmation, while force pushes, merges, and destructive actions remain guarded.

changes.label: Windows
changes.text: Settings saves now retry brief file locks from antivirus, indexing, or another app instance instead of failing immediately.

changes.label: Sidebar
changes.text: In the flat thread list, main-branch rows now show Files and Terminal controls the same way worktree rows do.

changes.label: Crossagents
changes.text: Crossagents only spawn subagents after you explicitly ask in that thread — for example with an @Crossagents mention — and that ask covers later turns in the same thread.

changes.label: Qwen
changes.text: Current Alibaba Token Plan models, including Qwen3.7 Max, Qwen3.7 Plus, Qwen3.6 Flash, and DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731, are detected and labeled correctly.

releases.title: A models home inside Settings, self-naming threads & a zoom pill
releases.summary: Everything about providers, quota and crafting now lives in one “Models & management” section inside Settings, threads name themselves with the agent actually running them, and pressing Ctrl +/-/0 surfaces a small pill that shows — and adjusts — the current zoom.

changes.label: Settings
changes.text: A new “Models & management” group sits at the top of the Settings sidebar and gathers channels & quota, model management, usage stats, the harness overview, and the crafting workbench behind one door — the sidebar's merged footer button and every existing usage shortcut now land there.

changes.label: Zoom
changes.text: Adjusting the app zoom pops a small pill under the titlebar showing the current percentage with −/+ and Reset controls, so the scale you're at is always obvious.

changes.label: Threads
changes.text: Threads created with a default title now get a summary from the agent actually running the session — falling back to other available agents — so sidebar names match the harness you picked.

changes.label: Sidebar
changes.text: Project names show in full by default: the pin, new-chat and more-actions buttons only claim space while your pointer is over the row, and the merged footer button reads “Models & management / Open settings”.

changes.label: Home
changes.text: Recent threads are grouped under their project on the home screen and limited to threads updated in the last three days, keeping the list focused on work you're actually returning to.

The standalone home page merged into the draft composer — mascot and greeting up top, projects and recent threads in the middle, composer at the bottom — and the “New” menu is trimmed to just New chat and New project with a panel that matches the composer surface.

changes.label: Models & usage
changes.text: Ctrl +/− zoom no longer squeezes the provider grid into single-character columns — cards drop to two columns when the panel gets too narrow and grow back to four as it widens.

releases.title: Flat thread list, worktree moves, workspaces & OpenCode sign-in fixes
releases.summary: The sidebar can now show every project's threads in one flat, filterable list, and you can move an existing thread into a worktree straight from its context menu. Remote-paired projects, Kimi Code sessions, Factory Droid subagents, and Windows agent launches are all more dependable. Signing into OpenCode through the new console finally registers — the session cookie it issues is recognized — and Command Code's model list stops auto-expanding as upstream adds models.

changes.label: Sidebar
changes.text: Switch the thread list to a flat layout that shows every project's threads together, tagged by project and with Git status on each row, plus per-project filters.

changes.label: Sidebar
changes.text: The collapsed rail now has Browser and New thread buttons, and right-clicking a thread there opens the same context menu as the expanded sidebar.

changes.label: Worktrees
changes.text: Move an existing thread into a new worktree from its context menu, either clean or carrying its uncommitted changes along.

changes.label: Workspaces
changes.text: The project switcher groups projects by workspace, remembers the last project you used in each one, and follows you when you open a thread from another workspace.

changes.label: Cursor
changes.text: Cursor SDK chat gains the standard composer slash commands for model, effort, fast mode, plan mode, and agent selection.

changes.label: Plans
changes.text: When an ACP agent proposes a plan, the full plan shows in the approval request so you can read it before you accept, and plan mode stays in sync when the agent switches modes on its own.

changes.label: Pull requests
changes.text: The PR automation control now shows a distinct icon and label for Auto Fix and Auto Merge so the selected mode is clear at a glance.

changes.label: Kimi
changes.text: Kimi Code handles workspace trust, signing out, thinking levels, question dialogs, and background tasks much more reliably, and a resumed thread now waits on 0.34's cache-expiry dialog instead of answering it by accident.

changes.label: Factory
changes.text: Factory Droid subagent transcripts now stream dependably into the parent thread, and built-in HTTP MCP servers reach Droid sessions.

changes.label: Remote
changes.text: Mirrored projects are labeled with their server across the sidebar and project switcher, their threads launch on the host machine and reopen dependably, and you can move a remote thread into a worktree from the desktop or your phone.

changes.label: Settings
changes.text: A single Prevent sleep policy in General settings replaces the old scattered toggles — keep the machine awake while agents are working, while remote access is enabled, or always.

changes.label: Editor
changes.text: Overflowing editor tabs scroll horizontally with the mouse wheel, and the active tab is always scrolled into view.

changes.label: Qwen
changes.text: Your saved Qwen model selections move from the retired Qwen 3.8 Max Preview to the released Qwen 3.8 Max.
Idle Files and Terminal buttons on sidebar rows now tuck away until you hover, and workflow actions in the GitHub Actions view stand out better on hover.

changes.label: Windows
changes.text: Agent commands containing quotes, newlines, or shell metacharacters now launch correctly through WSL and PowerShell instead of failing to parse.
A thread marked done stays done when you open it, and a worktree group collapses once its last thread is marked done.

changes.label: Remote
changes.text: Pasted images now show a preview and reach the agent on remote threads, and threads created on the host no longer disappear during sync.
Provider usage keeps reporting after a browser sign-in rotates its cookies, duplicated question headers are gone, and the model visibility list no longer overflows the window.

Closing the last browser tab no longer leaves the right panel stuck on a blank browser view, the side panel border no longer shifts the layout when it closes, and project settings open without a brief empty flash.

changes.label: OpenCode
changes.text: Browser sign-in to opencode.ai/console now captures the `console_session` cookie the new console actually issues, so a completed login is detected instead of looping until it times out.

changes.label: OpenCode
changes.text: Accounts redirected from the legacy console to the new console (billing migration) are recognized as signed in rather than reported as missing credentials, and the session validator now checks both console surfaces.

changes.label: Command Code
changes.text: The model picker no longer grows on its own when the upstream catalog adds models — newly discovered entries stay hidden until you opt them in.

releases.title: Remote machines, GitHub Actions, PR automation & speed tiers
releases.summary: CraftStation now runs agents on remote machines over SSH, manages GitHub Actions, and automates pull request fixes and merges. This release also adds project workspaces, configurable Crossagents routing, structured Cursor SDK chat, goal controls for Codex and Grok, tiered Fast/Ultrafast speed lanes with GPT-6.1 Sol, a dedicated Harness map, and performance and reliability improvements.

changes.label: Remote
changes.text: Connect a machine from your SSH config to install the CraftStation runtime and run agents, clone repositories, open threads and terminals, and review Git while project data remains on the remote machine.

changes.label: Remote
changes.text: Remote machines report their reachability in the sidebar, block launches while offline, support per-project sync and host updates, and can keep your desktop awake while remote access is enabled.

changes.label: GitHub
changes.text: Use the GitHub Actions view to pin and browse workflows, dispatch runs with inputs, rerun, cancel, or delete runs, and inspect job and step status from pull request checks.

changes.label: Pull requests
changes.text: PR automation monitors a pull request, fixes failed checks, merges with your selected method, marks the thread done, and shows live PR status in the thread's changes bubble.

changes.label: Workspaces
changes.text: Group projects into named workspaces and switch the sidebar between them.

changes.label: Crossagents
changes.text: Configure delegation routing in settings by ranking providers by usage, favorites, and tags; pinning overrides; pausing providers; hiding models; and editing learned routing data.

changes.label: Crossagents
changes.text: Delegated agents can run in the background and notify you after the parent turn becomes idle.

changes.label: Providers
changes.text: Cursor now supports structured SDK chat alongside CLI and ACP modes, with a default runtime setting, per-thread selection from the model menu, and managed installation and updates.

changes.label: Goals
changes.text: Codex threads now support edit, pause, resume, and clear goal controls from the composer on desktop and PWA, while Grok supports goal tracking and subagent work.

changes.label: Experiments
changes.text: AI judging can grade captured, anonymized chat responses instead of comparing only diffs.

changes.label: Git review
changes.text: Add an inline comment to any diff line to place it and its context in the composer as a fix prompt.

changes.label: Fast mode
changes.text: Models that offer more than one speed lane now show a tiered Fast mode submenu — pick Fast or Ultrafast where available — and the composer pill names the lane you picked.

changes.label: Codex
changes.text: GPT-6.1 Sol appears in the Codex model list and becomes the default when your Codex CLI provides it (codex-cli 0.159.x or newer).

changes.label: Workbench
changes.text: The crafting workbench gains a dedicated Harness map — a tree of your selected channel with a repointable compatibility trunk — split out from the recipes rail.

changes.label: Layout
changes.text: Tool rails can attach to either edge of a thread, side panels can lock to threads, floating right panels and the bottom terminal are resizable, and sidebar footer shortcuts are configurable.
Thread plans now dock in the right panel alongside Git and terminals, and diff counters animate as numbers change.

changes.label: Performance
changes.text: Idle resource use is lower: the composer avoids continuous GPU work, Git polling backs off, and terminal panels prewarm for faster opening.

changes.label: Git
changes.text: Pull with rebase now stashes and reapplies local changes, preserving the stash if reapplication conflicts.

changes.label: Remote
changes.text: Remote sessions now render remote-hosted images in chat and preserve previews when uploading clipboard pastes and staged attachments.

changes.label: PWA
changes.text: The PWA groups completed threads into a Done section, identifies the paired desktop in the wide sidebar, and uses lighter iOS transitions for fullscreen pages.

changes.label: Command Code
changes.text: Command Code now reuses CLI credentials across native and WSL environments and reports OAuth usage in provider stats.
A recovery screen now provides update and migration options when the database cannot open after an update.

changes.label: Remote
changes.text: Pairing links refresh before they expire, the PWA recovers from stale cached assets after a deployment, and unresponsive SSH machines are marked offline instead of leaving projects stuck loading.
Virtual chat rows no longer overlap after growing mid-list, the transcript stays pinned to the bottom while the composer resizes, and tool groups re-pin correctly on touch screens.
Replacement Codex sessions survive teardown, pending agent questions recover after a remote reconnect, and agent-initiated follow-up turns no longer remain stuck open.

changes.label: Usage
changes.text: Usage reporting is more accurate and reliable: exhausted plans show zero credits, empty Codex credit cards stay hidden, and Grok CLI tokens refresh before they expire.

changes.label: Windows
changes.text: Agent detection resolves Scoop shims correctly, and Cursor probes and launches without the cmd wrapper.
Built-in agent updates verify the installed version before reporting failure, and native and WSL environments track available updates independently.

changes.label: Fast mode
changes.text: New threads start on Standard speed again — Fast is a per-thread opt-in — and the switch now appears for custom Kimi models and channel models whose runtime honors service tiers, sending the correct catalog tier id on every turn instead of silently falling back.

changes.label: Usage
changes.text: Quota cards no longer flash unknown resets or token placeholders, and account pools lay out four cards per row again.

changes.label: Notifications
changes.text: A notification on the thread you are already watching is marked read instead of lingering in the inbox.

releases.title: Real brand logos for MiniMax, Muse, Step Code, and Devin
releases.summary: Four providers that showed letter placeholders now wear their official marks, vendored from each vendor's own site.

changes.label: Branding
changes.text: MiniMax, Muse, Step Code, and Devin badges now use the official favicons from minimax.io, about.meta.com, stepfun.com, and devin.ai instead of generic letter tiles.

changes.label: Branding
changes.text: Badge tiles are tuned per mark: dark tiles behind white-on-transparent logos (Devin, StepFun) and brand tiles behind colored marks, so every provider reads at a glance.

releases.title: A Fast toggle you can actually see, and the real Grok fast model
releases.summary: Fast mode is now a labeled switch next to the model and effort pickers, Grok folds its true fast catalog id into one toggle, and custom channels can be removed from the model manager.

changes.label: Composer
changes.text: Fast mode now shows as a labeled toggle beside the model list and reasoning strength — previously it was a bare icon-only button that was easy to miss entirely.

changes.label: Grok
changes.text: Grok's fast tier is the real advertised id (grok-4.7-build-fast). It now folds into Grok 4.7's Fast switch and is what actually launches — no more phantom grok-4.7-fast row.

changes.label: Model management
changes.text: Selecting a custom API channel now offers a 删除渠道 action with confirmation, which removes the account credential and its custom models together.

releases.title: Sign-in that survives restarts, and a completion card that dismisses itself
releases.summary: Antigravity and Step Code credentials are now recognized across restarts, Step Code joins the channels & usage list, and the Workspace inbox completion card clears on its own while you are watching the thread.

changes.label: Workspace
changes.text: The completion card on a thread you are already watching now disappears on its own — finishing a task no longer leaves a stuck unread notice until you switch threads.

changes.label: Accounts
changes.text: Antigravity and Step Code no longer appear signed out after a restart. Antigravity reads credentials parked in managed account-pool buckets, and Step Code reads the auth file written by step login directly.

changes.label: Channels & Usage
changes.text: A signed-in Step Code shows up as a channel you can manage, and its usage card reports your identity (plan name + masked account id). Step Plan has no public quota API, so the card shows identity rather than invented meters.

changes.label: Accounts
changes.text: Removing the Step Code authorization now also clears the step entry from the local CLI credential files, so the login cannot resurrect on the next refresh.

releases.title: A Fast toggle for Codex, Kimi, and Grok
releases.summary: Models with an official fast lane now offer a Fast switch in the model picker — Codex priority tier, Kimi HighSpeed, and Grok's fast variants, all off by default until you opt in.

changes.label: Models
changes.text: The model picker gains a Fast toggle on models that genuinely support one: Codex requests run on the official fast service tier, kimi-for-coding switches to kimi-for-coding-highspeed, and Grok's fast model variants collapse into a single Fast choice on the base model. Fast defaults to off and is remembered per model once you enable it.

changes.label: Models
changes.text: Fast can never fabricate a model id — a saved Fast flag on a model with no official variant degrades to the normal model instead of inventing names like k3-fast, and switching agents drops Fast when the target model has no fast lane.

releases.title: Usage sessions that heal themselves & a Step Code sign-in
releases.summary: Provider cards no longer get stuck on "signed in but no quota" — dead stored sessions renew automatically from the live browser session, and Step Code joins the sign-in channel list.

changes.label: Usage
changes.text: OpenCode could show "已登录" with "暂无额度窗口" forever: a mid-login placeholder cookie overwrote the good snapshot and nothing repaired it on the read path. Cookie mirroring now validates before sealing, and provider cards silently renew a dead stored session — harvesting the live browser session first — before ever asking you to sign in again.

changes.label: Usage
changes.text: Step Code now appears in the sign-in channel list. Its 登录/授权 button runs the native `step login` terminal flow — the same entry the Harness panel offers — so the Step credential lands in ~/.stepcode/auth.json where the harness reads it.

releases.title: Step Code routes by what the channel can speak
releases.summary: Step-family third-party models no longer crash into an incompatible-harness error — channels proven Chat Completions-capable run on native Step Code, everything else falls back to OpenCode automatically.

changes.label: Harness
changes.text: Step-family third-party models picked Step Code even when the step binary was missing or the channel was Responses-only, which failed at bind time. Routing now checks the installed harnesses and each channel's wire surface, so incapable picks land on OpenCode instead of an error.

changes.label: Harness
changes.text: Channel verification now also probes /chat/completions once and seals the result with the account credential. A Responses-first channel that still serves Chat Completions runs Step Code natively; the send path lazily probes once per channel when the stamp is missing.

releases.title: Provider usage credentials that stay signed in
releases.summary: Usage-panel credentials now survive updates and restarts — OpenCode renews dead session cookies silently, and Antigravity accounts keep showing quota when their windows roll back to full.

changes.label: Usage
changes.text: OpenCode and Command Code quota no longer demand a fresh login after every update or restart — expired session cookies are renewed silently from the persistent browser session, with a hidden re-auth pass before the sign-in window ever appears.

changes.label: Usage
changes.text: Antigravity accounts no longer report "no quota record" the moment a Gemini or Claude window rolls back to full — nominal full buckets render as 0% used, and a running Antigravity session contributes its official language-server quota when its email matches the account.

releases.title: Step Code as a first-class native harness
releases.summary: StepFun's Step Code CLI is now fully wired into CraftStation — it shows up in the Harness & CLI panel, the workbench, and CLI update checks, and Step-family models pick it automatically.

changes.label: Harnesses
changes.text: Step Code is now a first-class native harness — install it from the Harness & CLI panel, select it in the workbench, and pair it with Step-family models through a native recipe.

changes.label: CLI updates
changes.text: Step Code participates in CLI update checks, with latest-version detection powered by StepFun's official release manifest.
Step-family models no longer fall back to OpenCode when Step Code is installed — Auto routes them to the Step Code native harness.

releases.title: Workspace shortcuts, project pins & archived projects
releases.summary: Threads you are still working on, that stopped on an error, or that finished unread now also show up in a Workspace section. The original row stays in its project — Workspace is another way in, not a second thread.

changes.label: Sidebar
changes.text: A Workspace section lists working, error-interrupted, and unread finished threads while each one remains under its own project. Opening either row opens the same thread.

changes.label: Sidebar
changes.text: Hover a project and pin it to the top of the project list. Pin it again to put it back. Workspace itself starts pinned above the projects, and you can unpin that section so it sits next to Home.

changes.label: Sidebar
changes.text: Archiving a project removes it from the project list instead of leaving a faded row. Expand Archive at the bottom of the sidebar and use Enable Project to bring it back.
GitHub releases include both a portable build and an installer for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

releases.title: In-turn waits for agents, safer Codex auth & full access by default
releases.summary: Agents in any harness can now block inside a turn until a terminal pane prints something or a file under the worktree changes. Managed Codex profiles stop leaking platform API keys into ChatGPT subscription calls, and new threads default to Full Access.

changes.text: Agents can call the new wait tool inside a turn — it blocks until a timeout or a watched signal fires: new output on an integrated terminal pane (optionally matching a pattern), a pane exiting, or a file create/modify/delete under the worktree. Monitoring loops no longer spend a shell call per poll.
New threads — created by you or by another agent — now default to the permission level set under Settings → General, which ships as Full Access.

changes.label: Codex
changes.text: Managed Codex profiles no longer leak a service-account API key into ChatGPT subscription requests — the sk-… 401 loop on chatgpt.com is gone, and CODEX_API_KEY / CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN in the environment can no longer hijack a managed session.
Switching projects no longer discards the prompt you were still drafting — the composer text moves with you to the new project.

releases.title: Step Code support, live file previews & Codex fixes
releases.summary: StepFun's Step Code joins the provider list with its own models and sign-in. File previews refresh when a file changes on disk, and Codex threads stop showing "working" after the turn already ended.

changes.label: Step Code
changes.text: StepFun's Step Code agent is now a supported provider — install it from Settings, sign in from the terminal, and chat in structured sessions that default to step-5-preview.

changes.label: Step Code
changes.text: Third-party OpenAI-compatible accounts with a custom Base URL and API key can drive Step Code sessions, and existing Step Code sessions are discovered and can be resumed.

changes.label: File preview
changes.text: PDFs, images, videos, and Office documents open in the file panel now reload when the file changes on disk, so an agent's edits show up instead of a stale copy.

changes.label: Codex
changes.text: A Codex or ChatGPT thread no longer stays stuck on "working" when the app server ends the turn through an abort, an error, or an idle status instead of a completion event.

releases.title: Each thread keeps its files, formulas render
releases.summary: The files you open stay with that conversation, and Markdown preview typesets display formulas instead of showing the raw TeX.

changes.text: Open files, the project the file list points at, and whether the directory is hidden now stay with the current thread. Switching conversations no longer shows a PDF you opened somewhere else.
Hiding the directory affects only that thread. It stays hidden when you leave and come back, and other threads keep their own directory.
Markdown preview typesets display formulas instead of leaving the $$ source on the page. Inline math in a table header no longer shifts the score cells.

releases.title: Clearer quota and a live thinking trail
releases.summary: Account quota now follows the window that actually blocks the next turn, and the thinking trail stays open while the agent is still working.

changes.text: Quota for Codex, Grok, Kimi, Antigravity, and OpenAI-compatible channels follows the rate window that blocks the next turn. A single model carve-out, extra-usage charge, or reset-credit counter no longer marks the whole account empty.
When another account still has room, CraftStation skips one that is already low. If every account is low, it picks the one with the most remaining on that blocking window.
The live thinking and tool trail stays expanded so you can see the latest steps. Finished trails stay collapsed.

releases.title: Custom models stay on their account
releases.summary: Restarting CraftStation no longer drops the account behind a custom model. StepFun step-5-preview and similar models load their own config again, and a thread that drifted onto another harness comes back when you send.

changes.text: After a restart, a custom model such as StepFun step-5-preview uses the account you already configured, instead of failing with Model not found.
Sending that model from a thread that was moved to another harness, such as Devin, returns to OpenCode and the same account instead of asking the other harness to run it.

releases.title: Update downloads no longer sit at 0%
releases.summary: A slow update check no longer leaves the titlebar on Downloading… 0% with a button that does nothing. The download starts once a newer version is found, and a stalled 0% pill opens the release page in the browser.

changes.label: Updates
changes.text: Finding a new version after a slow check still starts the download, instead of leaving Downloading… 0% with nothing in progress.

changes.label: Updates
changes.text: The download pill stays clickable. At 0% with no bytes yet it offers a browser download, instead of ignoring the click.

releases.title: Titlebar shortcuts reach the version, status opens in one click
releases.summary: Pinned titlebar shortcuts now run across to the version pill instead of stopping halfway. The project status capsule opens the full Git panel on the first click. Hiding the file list in the right sidebar stays hidden when you leave a thread and come back.

changes.label: Titlebar
changes.text: Pinned shortcuts now continue across the titlebar up to the version number, leaving the update badge and window buttons in place, instead of being cut off at the middle of the window.

changes.label: Status
changes.text: Clicking the project status capsule opens the full Git panel immediately, with changes, branch, and commit, instead of stopping on the title row until a second click.

changes.label: Files
changes.text: Hiding the file list in the right sidebar stays hidden when you leave the thread and come back.

releases.title: GPT-6 Sol from the official catalog & a ChatGPT reset you can spend
releases.summary: Fetching Codex models now reads the official ChatGPT catalog, so GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna show up when the installed CLI still lists the 5.6 names. A ChatGPT account with an unused reset card can spend it from the quota page.

changes.label: ChatGPT
changes.text: An unused reset card now shows on the account row, and you can spend that card from CraftStation. The weekly meter refreshes after the card is redeemed.

changes.label: Codex
changes.text: Fetch models now asks the official ChatGPT catalog with a signed-in pool account, so GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna appear even when the local Codex model list is still on the 5.6 names.

releases.title: Folded thoughts, steadier Devin turns & menus that stay put
releases.summary: Thinking now collapses with searches and views instead of filling the chat. Devin SWE-2 keeps working through a quiet gap, zoomed menus open on the row you clicked, and threads that share a workspace can see each other across harnesses.

changes.label: Chat
changes.text: Consecutive thoughts fold into the same collapsed summary as searches and views, so a run reads as a thought count instead of a stack of open thinking rows. Open the group to read each thought.

changes.label: Cross-thread
changes.text: Threads that share a workspace path can see and message each other across harnesses, including Devin, instead of only Codex threads in the same project.

changes.label: Devin
changes.text: SWE-2 no longer treats a quiet gap, or a cancelled stop you did not request, as Stop. A live command stays running until the turn actually finishes.

changes.label: Menus
changes.text: Right-click and overflow menus stay next to the row you clicked when CraftStation's zoom is not 100%.

releases.title: Directories collapse, side panels stay open
releases.summary: You can hide the project directory without closing the file you are reading, and switching threads no longer throws away an open browser or a file tree you just loaded. Finished replies also leave Working on every structured agent.

changes.label: Files
changes.text: You can collapse just the project directory beside a preview and bring that column back from a small restore chip. The file you are reading stays open.

changes.label: Files
changes.text: The directory header no longer shows the unused new-file, new-folder, collapse-all, and refresh buttons. Those actions stay on the right-click menu.
An open browser page and a project file tree stay ready when you switch threads or right-panel tabs, instead of reloading from scratch each time.

changes.label: Files
changes.text: Right-clicking a file or folder in the project tree opens its menu, instead of jumping the preview and then doing nothing.
Grok, Claude, and the other structured agents leave Working when the visible reply is finished, even if a background sub-agent is still open or never reports back.

releases.title: Turns finish on their own
releases.summary: Finished tasks return to idle, scheduled runs can stop themselves, and usage icons open usage statistics. Website downloads in mainland China come from Gitee.

changes.text: A finished turn now returns to idle after a mid-turn prompt or sub-agent, including Codex, Claude, and other structured agents, instead of leaving Stop and the working timer up.

changes.label: Schedules
changes.text: A scheduled run can pause or delete its own schedule from the last line of its reply, even when that harness has no Schedule tools.

changes.label: Usage
changes.text: The collapsed sidebar no longer repeats the title bar shortcuts. Usage and Settings stay on the title bar, and every usage icon opens Usage statistics.

changes.label: Downloads
changes.text: The Windows installer and portable build downloaded from the website come from Gitee in mainland China and from GitHub elsewhere. In-app updates still use the GitHub feed.

releases.title: Web push, richer ACP agents & smoother chat
releases.summary: Installed CraftStation web apps can now notify you when remote agents need attention, Qwen exposes its live goals, and Kimi and Qwen show background subagent work as it happens. A broad set of provider, chat, mobile, and browser refinements makes everyday sessions more reliable.

changes.label: Remote
changes.text: Installed CraftStation web apps can now receive push notifications from a paired desktop—even while suspended—when an agent finishes or needs input.

changes.label: Qwen Code
changes.text: Qwen Code now shows live goal progress with elapsed time, iterations, and completed, failed, or cancelled outcomes, and identifies regional Token Plan tiers so usage labels are accurate.

changes.label: ACP agents
changes.text: ACP subagent runs now appear as nested agent activity, and Kimi Code and Qwen Code background agents keep streaming progress and results after the foreground turn ends.

changes.label: Claude
changes.text: Claude profiles can now choose the effort levels exposed by each custom model, so external-provider models only offer tiers they actually support.

Provider integrations better match their current CLIs: Antigravity discovers available models and effort levels dynamically, keeps terminal choices in sync, and Kimi updates through its official non-interactive installer.

Markdown images now share preview, copy, and download controls—including local project images—while long chats stay anchored during streaming and iOS can leave a long thread without stalling on a history snapshot.

changes.label: CraftStation
changes.text: CraftStation's icon set is refreshed across desktop, tray, mobile, web, and browser surfaces, while the website gains a dedicated About page and clearer remote-pairing presentation.

Structured chats preserve a queued steer if an unresponsive provider must restart; Kimi questions select the intended answer, Qwen resumes work immediately after a reply, and late or duplicate ACP updates no longer corrupt settled turns.
Browser screenshots no longer include CraftStation's presence cursor or click ripple, and Codex can use CraftStation's Browser MCP without a conflicting browser skill overriding it.

changes.label: Security
changes.text: Known-vulnerable transitive versions of adm-zip, brace-expansion, protobufjs, and shell-quote are overridden with patched releases.

releases.title: Reliable Devin task completion
releases.summary: A focused hotfix prevents completed Devin sessions from remaining stuck in the working state after autonomous follow-up work finishes.

changes.label: Devin
changes.text: Threads now return to idle after Devin finishes autonomous work and sends its final response, while genuine follow-up activity keeps the working state active.

releases.title: MiniMax Code, ZCode & recoverable agent workflows
releases.summary: CraftStation adds native MiniMax Code and ZCode recipes, reduces the context cost of large MCP catalogs, and makes handoffs, workflow runs, artifacts, and context usage easier to recover and trust.

changes.label: MiniMax Code
changes.text: Run structured sessions through the official mcode acp runtime, with TUI and headless modes, session resume, MCP, Skills, installation guidance, and login detection.

changes.label: ZCode
changes.text: Use an experimental ZCode Recipe with the official terminal harness and GLM-5.3, including headless JSON, session resume, status reporting, permission recognition, and source-build installation guidance.

changes.label: MCP
changes.text: Large built-in tool catalogs can expose search and invoke tools first, allowing agents to discover capabilities in Chinese or English without loading every schema into context while preserving permission and input validation.

changes.label: Handoffs
changes.text: Agent handoffs retain the original goal, constraints, unanswered requests, blockers, and critical files with item anchors so the receiving session can continue with less reconstruction.

changes.label: Workflows
changes.text: Active workflow runs survive renderer restarts and now expose resume lineage, supersession, stop reasons, resumability, and WSL context.

changes.label: Artifacts
changes.text: Generated artifacts carry version, source, producer, attempt, validation, and status metadata separately from their content.

changes.label: Context
changes.text: Context usage reports its provider or local source, scope, measurement time, freshness, cache semantics, and compaction state in desktop and mobile views.

releases.title: Fable 5 weekly usage tracking
releases.summary: A focused patch for Claude usage tracking: the usage panel now shows your per-model weekly limits, including Claude Fable 5's, and Claude usage stays signed in and up to date.

changes.text: The Claude card in the usage panel now tracks per-model weekly limits, so you can watch your Claude Fable 5 weekly quota fill and reset alongside the session and overall weekly bars.
Claude usage keeps loading after your sign-in token expires — CraftStation now renews it automatically instead of showing a misleading “Not signed in”.

releases.title: Claude Fable 5 returns
releases.summary: A focused patch that brings Claude Fable 5 back to the model picker, with its frontier reasoning effort levels and one-million-token context window.

changes.text: You can now run Claude Fable 5 from the model picker again, with its frontier reasoning effort levels and a one-million-token context window.

releases.title: Claude Sonnet 5 with a 1M-token context
releases.summary: A focused update that brings Claude Sonnet 5 to the model picker, complete with its frontier reasoning effort levels and a one-million-token context window.

changes.text: You can now run Claude Sonnet 5 from the model picker, with its frontier reasoning effort levels and a one-million-token context window, once your Claude CLI is up to date.

releases.title: 组合架构统一、额度修复与资源优化
releases.summary: 统一 Item、Recipe、CraftPlan 与运行会话的契约，修复配方保存、权限传递、文件引用与账号授权管理。优化持久化、高亮缓存与 Windows 安装体积，保留现有功能及恢复路径。

changes.label: 性能
changes.text: 会话增量处理和 SQLite 写入减少重复工作，高亮缓存设定内存上限，Windows 安装内容减少约 33 MiB 的编译中间文件。

changes.label: Antigravity
changes.text: 账号池同时显示 Gemini 与 Claude 的 5 小时和周额度，不再漏掉周额度消耗。

changes.label: 账号授权
changes.text: 删除 Devin 授权会清理本机 CLI 凭据；删除失败会显示原因，旧额度请求也无法重新显示已删除账号。

changes.label: 合成台
changes.text: 兼容桥配方可确认保存，取消不会提前写入；自定义模型、第三方 API、可选 CPA 与目标 Harness 保持独立绑定。

changes.label: 权限
changes.text: 新建、恢复和后续消息统一传递默认权限，同时保留用户显式选择及各 CLI 的权限语义。

changes.label: 聊天
changes.text: Windows 聊天文件引用可正确打开，快速停止与重载续接不会重复发送或遗失终态。

changes.label: 持久化
changes.text: 用户消息可靠落盘并去除重复回显，修复多连接写入和协作队列竞争，保留重试与恢复能力。

releases.title: One-click setups for Z.ai, DeepSeek, and MiniMax
releases.summary: Claude Code Profiles gain ready-made presets that let you set up Z.ai (GLM), DeepSeek, and MiniMax with a single click. This release also keeps provider-specific model IDs intact and tidies up agent status when you remove a profile.

changes.text: You can now configure Z.ai (GLM), DeepSeek, and MiniMax with one click thanks to ready-made presets in your Claude Code Profiles.
Claude Code Profiles now seed a provider's environment and model configuration from a single menu, so you no longer have to enter it by hand.
External-provider model IDs such as glm-5.2 are now preserved exactly when launching Claude, so provider-specific suffixes are no longer stripped away.
Deleting a Claude profile now clears its agent status across native, WSL, and discovery lists, keeping what CraftStation detects in sync with your saved profiles.

releases.title: Multiple Claude profiles, a usage dashboard & glass sidebar
releases.summary: This release lets you run multiple Claude profiles with their own logins, models, and environments, adds a usage dashboard with a year-long activity heatmap, and gives the sidebar a translucent glass look. It also brings GitHub repo cloning, inline agent images, and smarter commit and PR actions.

changes.text: Set up multiple Claude profiles, each with its own login, model, reasoning effort, and environment variables, so you can switch between separate accounts and configurations.
Start a new project by cloning any GitHub repository directly from CraftStation.
Track your activity in a new usage dashboard featuring a 52-week heatmap, per-account filtering, and a breakdown of skill usage.
See images that agents generate rendered inline in the chat, with a hover toolbar for quick actions.
Enjoy a translucent glass sidebar with macOS vibrancy and tunable Windows acrylic frosting.
Choose how pull requests are created with a configurable PR creation mode, and refresh PR status on demand from the Git Review sidebar.
Commit and create PRs more easily with sticky commit actions in Git Review and clearer loading states for PR actions.
Work more smoothly in non-git projects and new worktrees, which now carry over your gitignored and uncommitted files.
Improved Command Code reliability by syncing its model picker with live models, fixing session resume, and quieting background updates during detection.

releases.title: Projects without git, notes panel, and Claude Fable 5
releases.summary: This release lets you create and open projects even when there's no git repository yet, adds a per-project notes and to-do panel, and brings support for Claude Fable 5. It also sharpens reliability for Claude on Windows and Codex turn handling.

changes.text: You can now create or open a project even when it isn't a git repository yet, with a unified setup flow that can initialize git for you on the spot.
A new per-project notes and to-do panel gives you a dedicated place to jot down reminders and track tasks alongside your work.
CraftStation now supports Claude Fable 5, so you can run the latest Claude model directly in your sessions.
Built-in browser windows now present a Chrome-like identity, so more websites load and behave correctly.
The git review panel now keeps its state as you move around the app, so you no longer lose your place when it remounts.
Starting Claude on Windows is far more reliable, with fixes for npm shim paths, slower job-helper startup, and stray startup errors.
Codex turns now complete cleanly even when the completion notification arrives without details, and pending output is flushed before a turn is marked idle.

releases.title: Provider usage tracking, Command Code, and rebuilt themes
releases.summary: A big feature release: track your provider quotas and usage for Claude Code, Codex, and more in one place, run the new Command Code CLI entirely inside CraftStation, and enjoy fully rebuilt light and dark themes. Git worktrees are faster with inline diffs and live status, and WSL and Windows support is stronger across the board.

changes.text: A new usage panel tracks your provider quotas and consumption across Claude Code, Codex, Command Code, Grok, and other providers so you always know where you stand.
Command Code joins as a built-in CLI provider that you can install, update, log in to, and resume sessions with entirely inside CraftStation.
You can now drag and drop file attachments straight into the composer instead of browsing for them.
Selectable theme presets let you pick a look you like, with the terminal palette automatically synced to match.
Live subagent progress and token usage now appear in the UI so you can follow exactly what your agents are doing.
Light and dark themes have been rebuilt from the ground up with better contrast and refined, theme-aware colors throughout.
Git worktrees are faster and richer, with inline diffs when opening changed files, live status summaries, and the ability to merge right from the Create PR flow.
WSL and Windows support is stronger for running agents, installing providers, and applying updates, including native Grok Build installs and npm-installed command shims.
Stuck or prematurely ended turns now recover reliably instead of leaving the conversation hung.
Codex sessions are more stable, with deduplicated errors, quieter resumes, and correct service-tier handling each turn.
Grok login and usage collection have been fixed so account status reports correctly.

releases.title: Smoother microphone access and wider file reach
releases.summary: A focused patch that smooths out microphone permissions and lets CraftStation open files beyond your active project, plus a fix for links to deeply nested paths.

changes.text: CraftStation now handles OS-level microphone permission gracefully and gives you a direct link to system settings when access needs to be granted.
You can now open and read files that live outside your active project root, so reference material elsewhere on your machine is just a click away.
Links to files with long or deeply nested paths no longer get truncated and now open the correct location every time.

releases.title: Grok Build, Opus 4.8 workflows, voice input & thread rollback
releases.summary: A big feature release: install and run Grok Build straight from the app, drive Claude Opus 4.8 with Ultracode effort and workflows, talk to your agents with local voice input, and undo an agent's work with thread rollback. Plus one-click agent installs, live GitHub PRs in-app, and more than 70 improvements and fixes.

changes.text: You can now install and run Grok Build directly from the app, no separate setup required.
Claude Opus 4.8 is available with the new Ultracode effort level and a redesigned workflow runner with trigger chips.
Local voice input lets you dictate prompts to your agents using on-device Whisper speech recognition, with audio settings to tune it.
Coding agents like Grok, Antigravity, and others now install with a single click using platform-native install paths.
Thread rollback lets you undo an agent's work and retry from an earlier point, with the agent session and file watchers automatically restored.
GitHub pull requests are now shown live inside the app, with check status that refreshes automatically as your PRs run.
You can install and uninstall hook plugins for your CLI agents straight from the settings UI.
An expanded built-in browser, available via an @Browser mention, lets agents navigate and extract pages, and a resizable browser drawer keeps it handy.
Settings have been reorganized into focused pages, and the sidebar now shows installed agent icons, completion states, and animated terminal activity at a glance.
Chat now renders Markdown tables, clickable links, read results, and subagent progress more clearly across Claude, Codex, and ACP agents.
Git and worktree workflows are smoother, with stashing on pull, automatic status refresh, randomized branch names, and cleaner branch and worktree cleanup.
Sign-in, install, and update flows for agents are more reliable, including terminal login handoff, version detection, and update progress.
Interrupted or replayed Claude turns no longer surface false failure states after a reconnect.
Terminal paste from the clipboard and pressing Escape to dismiss overlays now work as expected.

releases.title: CraftStation reaches its first stable release
releases.summary: The first stable public release of CraftStation, graduating from the 0.9.x betas into a polished build with refreshed chrome, smoother Browser MCP controls, and better multi-agent diff handling.

changes.text: CraftStation reaches its first stable public release, bringing the workspace-native experience for orchestrating Claude, Codex, Gemini, Grok, Command Code, and other coding agents out of beta.
The thread, home, and welcome screens have a refreshed look with cleaner rounded tabs, smoother project switching, and a more polished overall presentation.
Browser MCP controls now live right in the message composer with a clearer header-style indicator, so you can toggle browser access without leaving your conversation.
OpenCode threads now render multi-file unified diffs inline, making it easier to review changes that span several files at once.
Cancelling a request mid-stream no longer surfaces a spurious error in the composer, so stopping an agent stays quiet and clean.
